description: Handshake inputs an implementation must refuse (PROTOCOL.md sections 3.1, 3.2, and 4.4). These are transformations of a live handshake rather than fixed bytes, because no implementation should accept an injected scalar or sid (section 3.2, trap #1). Take an honest HELLO or REPLY, alter it as described, and the named side must refuse with the code given. The conformance harness (conformance/src/scenarios.js) performs each of them against an implementation under test.
source: Specified by PROTOCOL.md; the encodings below are ones some serializer could produce and the canonical form forbids.
canonicalCaps: Each token matches ^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,14}[a-z0-9])?$; the set is deduplicated, sorted bytewise ascending, and joined with "," (0x2c), at most 128 bytes in all; the empty set is zero bytes. v2 defines two tokens, "resume" and "stream". A peer's caps are refused unless they are exactly this encoding, and are hashed into the transcript verbatim.

transformations.name: a reflected confirmation
transformations.how: return the sender's own confirmS as CONFIRM

transformations.name: capabilities stripped from HELLO in transit
transformations.how: rewrite caps_r in HELLO to a canonical subset; the sender MACs what it received, the receiver what it sent

transformations.name: capabilities stripped from REPLY in transit
transformations.how: rewrite caps_s in REPLY to a canonical subset after confirmS was computed

transformations.name: non-canonical caps in HELLO
transformations.how: replace caps_r with each nonCanonicalCaps entry

transformations.name: non-canonical caps in REPLY
transformations.how: replace caps_s with each nonCanonicalCaps entry

transformations.name: a sealed frame where HELLO belongs
transformations.how: send frames-negative.json sealed.manifest as the first bytes

transformations.name: a wrong confirmS
transformations.how: flip one bit of confirmS in REPLY

transformations.name: a HELLO replayed on a second connection
transformations.how: send the same HELLO bytes on a second connection for the same nameplate

transformations.name: a fresh Ya under a sid already seen
transformations.how: a second connection's HELLO carrying the first one's sid

reflection.what: Over handshake.json's transcript, sid, and K, neither confirmation verifies as the other: they share a key and a transcript and differ only by role label.
